original_question: A group is said to be self-similar if it admits a faithful state-closed representation by automorphisms of a regular one-rooted m-tree for some m. Can a torsion-free finitely presented metabelian group which is self-similar contain a subgroup isomorphic to the restricted wreath product H = Z ≀ Z? It is known that Z≀Z itself is self-similar(A. C. Dantas, T. M. G. Santos, S. N. Sidki, J. Algebra, 567(2021), 564–581).
target_in_paper: Problem 21.41 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)" of Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook.
correct_elements: Your draft already reproduces the paper's official problem essentially verbatim. It correctly states the paper's definition of a self-similar group, the exact hypotheses on the ambient group (torsion-free, finitely presented, metabelian, self-similar), the target subgroup H = ℤ ≀ ℤ, and the contextual remark that ℤ ≀ ℤ itself is known to be self-similar.
missing_details: For fully stand-alone precision, specify that the parameter m is a positive integer.
If H is kept as notation, define it explicitly as the restricted wreath product H = ℤ ≀ ℤ; for maximal self-containment one may spell this out as (⊕_{n∈ℤ} ℤ) ⋊ ℤ with the shift action.
The paper presents this as an open problem (Problem 21.41), not as a conjecture or theorem.
refined_question: Can a torsion-free, finitely presented, metabelian group that is self-similar—in the sense that it admits a faithful state-closed representation by automorphisms of a regular one-rooted m-tree for some positive integer m—contain a subgroup isomorphic to the restricted wreath product H = ℤ ≀ ℤ?
justification: The arXiv identifier 1401.0300 is the evolving Kourovka Notebook, and your draft matches the official statement of Problem 21.41 almost word for word. There is no narrower nearby reformulation or explicitly proved equivalent version attached to this problem in the paper itself, so the most paper-faithful refinement is a minimally edited stand-alone restatement of that exact problem, preserving the definition of self-similarity and the subgroup ℤ ≀ ℤ that appears in the original wording.
